Subject: Post-demo: scope confirmation for obfuscated header & trace-id handling

Hi Tom / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Per our conversation I wanted to capture the narrow scope we agreed to validate during the trial so your security team can sign off quickly. High-level asks you called out:

- Ensure request/response logs do NOT contain raw PII (names, SSNs, emails) or PHI.
- Obfuscate or drop sensitive HTTP headers (Authorization, Cookie, X-Internal-Trace, X-Client-Token).
- Decide approach for trace IDs: retain ephemeral trace ids for debugging but store only hashed/opaque IDs in logs; provide a reversible mapping for customer-managed HSM if required.
- Configure retention: full logs for 7 days, aggregated metrics for 90 days; ability to trigger ad-hoc redaction on request.

Next steps we proposed on the call:
1) Redwood sends a short options doc (attachment) outlining three ways to handle headers/trace IDs (masking rules, tokenization, customer-managed HSM).
2) Your security team (Priya) to list must-have vs nice-to-have requirements by mid-week.
3) We stand up a limited POC (dedicated sandbox) with logging rules applied and share sample sanitized logs for review.

Attached: redwood-logging-options.pdf — quick comparison table + sample sanitized log lines.

If that matches your expectations, I can loop in Neha (security) and Karthik (solutions) to build the sandbox and run the sample ingestion.

Thanks,
Marcus

Thanks Marcus —

This is helpful. A few clarifying questions from our side before we finalize the must-haves:

1) Can Redwood confirm whether masking is applied at SDK/agent ingestion time or inside the hosted collector? We prefer ingestion-time masking to avoid storing raw headers anywhere in the pipeline.
2) For trace ids: we need the ability to map a trace id back to a full request for a 30-day window in case of incident investigations. Are the hashed/opaque ids reversible if we enable customer-managed keys?
3) Are request bodies sampled? If so, what sampling rate controls exist and can we exclude endpoints that touch PHI from sampling entirely?
4) Will you provide a deletion/redaction API that supports bulk redaction for subject access requests?

If you can answer these items, we can mark the must-haves vs nice-to-haves and get procurement involved.

Hi Priya / Marcus —

Thanks for these great questions. Quick answers and proposed configuration that we can implement in the sandbox POC:

1) Masking location: we support both ingestion-time SDK masking and server-side collector rules. Given your preference, we recommend SDK-side deterministic masking for headers and request metadata so raw values never reach our central immutable store. If you prefer agentless ingestion, we can run collector-side masking with a short retention staging area (7 days) and automatic scrub before persistence.

2) Trace IDs: we can store a hashed trace id by default (SHA-256) and, with customer-managed KMS, we support envelope encryption for a reversible mapping. That reversible mapping is stored in an encrypted key vault that you control. For POC we can demonstrate both: non-reversible hash vs reversible tokenization via HSM.

3) Sampling & exclusion: sampling is configurable per-route. We will exclude any endpoint you mark as PHI from sampling entirely. For non-PHI endpoints you can set a sampling pct (0.1% — 5%) and we provide a sampling audit log.

4) Redaction API: yes — we have a bulk redaction API (trigger by request id, user id, email) and a compliance workflow to scrub historical logs. Note that live request traces stored in the short staging buffer are deleted immediately after scrub. We'll provide runbook steps in the POC.

Proposed sandbox configuration for POC:
- Mode: SDK-side masking (recommended)
- Header rules: drop Authorization/Cookie, mask X-Client-Token to fixed-length hash, scrub any header that matches regex for emails/ssn patterns
- Trace-id: show both hashed-only and HSM-tokenized samples
- Retention: raw staging 7d (collector-only), persisted sanitized logs 90d, metrics 1yr
- Deliverables: sample sanitized log file, redaction API walkthrough, SOC/controls mapping doc

I'll attach the checklist with exact regexes and API endpoints we propose for the sandbox. Marcus — if that looks right, Karthik and I can provision the environment; estimated time to first sample logs: 3 business days.

Neha Kapoor
Security Engineering, Redwood Inference
